title: Lamprey FinServ POC — Latency & Cost Surface Scan
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures the results of a focused "latency surface" scan we ran for Lamprey Systems (regional financial services POC). The goal was to map out latency percentiles, throughput ceilings, and token-level cost across a set of deployment options (hosted small pool vs. dedicated 1xA100 vs. on-prem 4xA10G) under three representative workload shapes: account-summary queries (short, <60 tokens), policy-explanations (medium, 200–400 tokens), and regulatory-document extraction (long, 1k+ tokens).

Top-level findings:
- Short queries: hosted API on small dedicated pool consistently hit p50 ~18ms, p95 ~75ms with batching disabled; dedicated 1xA100 improved p95 to ~45ms under low contention and to ~80ms at steady 100 qps when KV cache miss rate was >=20%.
- Medium queries: dedicated 1xA100 at qps 40–80 gives best cost/latency tradeoff; on-prem 4xA10G achieves comparable tail latency for long sequences once KV warmup is accounted for, but incurs higher steady-state cost from reserved hardware and orchestration overhead.
- Long queries: throughput is limited primarily by token generation speed and memory eviction patterns; quantized 4-bit model variants reduced cost per 1k tokens by ~28% with median latency regression of ~8–12% depending on sequence length.

Test configuration (explicit):
- Client load generator: k6 with custom token-aware workload driver; single orchestrator controlling 5 traffic injectors across two AZs to avoid single-host bottlenecks.
- Models: open-llm-fiducial-v2 (base fp16), fiducial-v2-q4_0 (4-bit), and fiducial-v2-ct(compiler-tuned variant).
- Runtime: Redwood-hosted API (auto), Dedicated 1xA100 (pinned), On-prem 4xA10G via Redwood Private v0.9.3.
- Serving config knobs recorded: max_batch_tokens {128, 512, 1024}, max_batch_latency_ms {5,10,30}, kv_cache_enabled {true,false}, session_affinity {off, per-user}.
- Measurement windows: coldstart (first 100 requests after node start), warm steady-state (30m continuous at target qps), microburst (sudden +3x qps for 60s), and recovery (60s following microburst).

Representative metrics (aggregated):
- Short query workload (avg request length 42 tokens):
  - Hosted (small pool): p50 18ms, p95 75ms, p99 210ms, throughput 480 qps sustained, cost ~ $0.0045 per 1k tokens.
  - Dedicated 1xA100: p50 12ms, p95 45ms, p99 160ms at 100 qps steady; degrades to p95~80ms at 200 qps when batch sizes increase. Cost ~ $0.0038 per 1k tokens (amortized reserved cost).
  - On-prem 4xA10G: p50 15ms, p95 55ms, p99 190ms, throughput tapers at 520 qps due to host-level NIC saturation observed in traces. Cost model: internal chargeback ~ $0.0056 per 1k tokens (includes infra ops).

- Medium query workload (avg request 320 tokens):
  - Dedicated 1xA100: p50 145ms, p95 430ms, p99 1020ms at 60 qps. Best steady tradeoff when max_batch_tokens=512 and kv_cache_enabled=true. Cost ~ $0.018 per 1k tokens.
  - On-prem 4xA10G: p50 170ms, p95 500ms after initial warmup; observed multi-tenant interference when background batch jobs scheduled. Cost model ~ $0.022 per 1k tokens.
  - Hosted: p50 210ms, p95 650ms; good for bursty developer traffic but more expensive at scale (cost ~ $0.026 per 1k tokens).

- Long query workload (avg request 1,200 tokens generative/extractive):
  - Quantized variant (q4): median tokens/sec improved by 22% vs fp16; p95 latency improved for sustained streams because token throughput increases but p50 sometimes slightly higher due to compile overhead.
  - Memory churn: on the on-prem cluster, eviction/reload events correlated with spikes in p99 (1.8–2.4x). Suggest increasing per-host model cache allocation or session affinity for sticky-heavy flows.

Anomalies and notes observed during runs:
- Coldstart tail: first-connection coldstarts were >2s on hosted pool when model was evicted; mitigations: keepalive pool, proactive pre-warm on deployment rollout, or cached model pinning on dedicated nodes.
- Microburst behavior: at +3x qps microbursts, we saw transient queueing that pushed p95 to 2–3x baseline. Queue drain time depended on max_batch_latency_ms: lower batch latency knobs reduced tail but cut throughput efficiency.
- Tokenization skew: ~6% of requests had unusual tokenization (customer text included long unicode blobs), increasing average token count and causing unexpected KV cache miss patterns. Recommend pre-tokenization validation in gateway.

Operational recommendations (for Lamprey):
1) Short-term (30–60 days): recommend Dedicated 1xA100 for core customer-facing endpoints (account-summary, quick-sentiment). Configure kv_cache_enabled=true and session_affinity=per-user to maximize warm cache hit. Set max_batch_tokens=128, max_batch_latency_ms=10 for latency-sensitive routes.
2) Medium-term (60–180 days): for policy-explanations and regulatory work, run dedicated autoscaler with burst pool capacity (Hosted fallback) and enable quantized model variants for long-running pipelines. Add pre-warm hooks in CI/CD to avoid deployment coldstarts.
3) Cost controls: apply token-level throttles and per-route cost buckets in the console; for predictable billing, a reserved Dedicated commit reduces unit cost by ~15–25% vs fully hosted at target qps ranges outlined above.
4) On-prem suggestions: if Lamprey wants max isolation, 4xA10G nodes are viable but require stricter orchestration: isolate inference lanes, increase NIC provisioning, and set node-level QoS to avoid batch-job interference.

Runbook snippets (quick):
- If p95 for short queries >120ms and utilization on dedicated node <70%: check kv cache hit rate, restart model worker with higher cache allocation, inspect inter-host NIC metrics.
- If throughput drops under microburst and queue lengths rise: increase burst capacity (hosted fallback), temporarily raise max_batch_latency_ms to 30ms then ramp down after drain.
- If unusual tokenization spikes appear: capture offending payloads via sampled request logs, apply pre-tokenizer to sanitize or truncate blobs, add a rate-limiter for oversized payloads.

Next experiments to run (proposal):
- Controlled warmup cadence: measure time-to-stable p95 after model rollout with a scripted warmup traffic (varying warmup intensity).
- Session affinity sensitivity: ramp up mixed-user flows with and without affinity to quantify global cache hit improvement and tail latency tradeoffs.
- Quantization safety sweep: A/B quality and hallucination regression tests on q4 variants against a focused set of Lamprey regulatory prompts.

Appendix: quick topline tables (CSV-like)
- Short workload summary:
  mode, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, qps_sustained, cost_per_1k_tokens
  hosted-small, 18, 75, 210, 480, $0.0045
  dedicated-1xA100, 12, 45, 160, 420, $0.0038
  onprem-4xA10G, 15, 55, 190, 520, $0.0056

- Medium workload summary:
  mode, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, qps_sustained, cost_per_1k_tokens
  dedicated-1xA100, 145, 430, 1020, 60, $0.018
  onprem-4xA10G, 170, 500, 1300, 56, $0.022
  hosted, 210, 650, 1500, 50, $0.026

Action items (owners):
- Maya: finalize presentation deck for Lamprey exec readout (due 2029-02-24).
- Priya: run quantization safety sweep (start 2029-02-21, initial results due 2029-03-05).
- Liam: add warmup step to the deployment pipeline and draft runbook page (due 2029-03-01).
- Zhao: capture packet traces on on-prem runs and investigate NIC saturation (due 2029-02-28).

Open questions for Lamprey engineering:
- What is acceptable p95 for short customer interactions during peak hours (we used 100ms as our internal threshold during tests)?
- Are there regulatory constraints on using quantized weights for audit trails?

Raw artifacts location: GitHub PR (benchmarks), Linear ticket LMP-1423, Confluence spec (lamprey-poc-spec-2029).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Observed subtle compiler jitter on fiducial-v2-ct at sequence boundaries; follow up with runtime team.
- Consider adding a small synthetic workload to mimic tokenization-skew inputs to the standard test harness so future runs catch it fast.

End of note.
